statement.p: Based on the graphs of f(x) and g(x) below, answer the following questions. You should not approximate any of your answers.

image.shortdescription: Graph of two functions and some points on the functions.

description.p: Function f starts at the origin, goes up and back down to the x-axis and then up higher and then back down to the axis again, with the two peaks at x=2.2 and x=6.1. It hits the x-axis at x=0, x=4, and x=8. Function g is an increasing line going though the points occuring at the two peaks of f, that is, (2.2, f(2.2)) and (6.1,f(6.1)).

statement.p: a) What is the average rate of change of f(x) over the interval \ 2.2 \leq x \leq 6.1 \ ?
b) What is the average rate of change of g(x) over the interval \ 2.2 \leq x \leq 6.1 \ ?

solution.p: The average rate of change of a function f(x) over an interval a \leq x \leq b is computed using the following formula: \mbox{Average Rate of Change of f(x) over } a \leq x \leq b = \frac{ \Delta f }{\Delta x} = \frac{ f(b) - f(a)}{b-a}

a) Using the formula above with the endpoints (2.2, 2.9) and ( 6.1, 4.9 ) we obtain the following answer: \mbox{Average Rate of Change of f(x) over } 2.2 \leq x \leq 6.1 = \frac{ 4.9 - 2.9}{6.1 - 2.2} = \frac{ 2}{3.9}

b) Using the formula above with the endpoints (2.2, 2.9) and ( 6.1, 4.9 ) we obtain the following answer: \mbox{Average Rate of Change of g(x) over } 2.2 \leq x \leq 6.1 = \frac{ 4.9 - 2.9}{6.1 - 2.2} = \frac{2}{3.9}
